lineage_context.teaching_goal: Use the tubular persistent calyx, stamens opposite petals and single-ovule ovary to distinguish the non-core Caryophyllales plumbago lineage.

project_scope.note: The sole project taxon is an introduced horticultural species native to China, so this family is primarily a crew/lookalike lesson rather than a native-family anchor.

family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: Look for a 5-part flower with a tubular/ribbed persistent calyx, 5 stamens positioned opposite the petals, and a superior one-celled ovary with a single ovule.
family_diagnostics.vegetative: Herbs, small shrubs or climbers; leaves simple, often basal or alternate; salt/mucilage-secreting glands are common in the family.
family_diagnostics.reproductive: Flowers usually bisexual and 5-merous. Calyx tubular or funnel-shaped and persistent; corolla 5-lobed; 5 stamens are opposite rather than alternating with the petals.
family_diagnostics.fruit: A one-seeded fruit, indehiscent or opening irregularly/by a lid depending on lineage, usually retained inside the persistent calyx.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: Opposite-the-petals stamens + persistent ribbed calyx + one ovule is the technical family door.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: 5-part flower → tubular persistent calyx → opposite stamens → one-seeded fruit → Polygonaceae comparison
visual_lesson.intro: Plumbaginaceae is a small project family, but it teaches an excellent botanical character: stamens opposite the petals.

steps.title: 1 · Inspect the calyx
steps.look_for: A narrow persistent calyx tube, often distinctly ribbed and sometimes glandular.
steps.why_it_matters: The calyx remains with the fruit and is a strong family clue.

steps.title: 2 · Check stamen position
steps.look_for: Five stamens aligned opposite the five petals/corolla lobes.
steps.why_it_matters: This is an unusually useful technical character for the family.

steps.title: 3 · Remember the project role
steps.look_for: Hardy plumbago is a rhizomatous horticultural perennial, not a Central Texas native anchor.
steps.why_it_matters: Prevents the family lesson from being mistaken for native-range endorsement.

comparisons.title: Plumbaginaceae vs Polygonaceae
comparisons.rule: Both are nearby Caryophyllales lineages. Polygonaceae commonly has an ocrea and angled nut; Plumbaginaceae lacks the ocrea and instead has a tubular persistent calyx and 5 stamens opposite the petals.

comparisons.title: Plumbaginaceae vs Primulaceae
comparisons.rule: Both can have stamens opposite petals, but Plumbaginaceae typically has a persistent ribbed calyx, one ovule/one seed and often secretory glands; Primulaceae generally has several to many seeds.

visual_lesson.caveat: The sole project species is introduced; the lesson is for recognition and horticultural comparison, not native-family prioritization.

genera.fast_cue: blue 5-part flower + persistent tubular calyx; horticultural groundcover habit
